findings.title: Develop Strategy to Address Going Concern Issue
findings.description: The Commission has a potential going concern issue as it does not have resources to continue operating without using reserve funds. During fiscal year 2016, the Commission used $70,000 in cash restricted for future projects to cover operating expenses and had a deficit of approximately $90,000 for restricted funds at year-end.

dollar_amounts.context: cash restricted for future projects used to cover operating expenses
deficit for restricted funds at end of fiscal year 2016
cost of two heating and air conditioning units

findings.recommendation: The Commission needs to research ways to increase revenues and evaluate in detail where they can reduce expenses. The Commission also needs to evaluate new projects in light of their mission and purpose.

findings.title: Improve Financial Recording
findings.description: The Commission does not have accounting personnel with adequate knowledge to properly record transactions. Errors included expensing capital assets instead of capitalizing them and incorrect handling of retiree healthcare liability accounts resulting in an overstatement of $35,060.

dollar_amounts.context: cost of two HVAC units expensed rather than capitalized
overstatement of liability and expense accounts
portion of overstatement from prior periods
portion of overstatement relating to fiscal year 2016
prior period adjustment for Oyster Management Reserve accounting

findings.recommendation: The Commission should provide the Administrative Assistant with appropriate training in proper accounting standards and hire a replacement with experience. The Executive Secretary should also ensure adequate knowledge of accounting procedures.

findings.title: Prepare Bank Reconciliations Timely
findings.description: During fiscal year 2016, the Commission did not prepare bank reconciliations timely for all accounts. The Assistant Executive Secretary prepared reconciliations sixty to ninety days after month end for a significant portion of accounts.
findings.recommendation: The Commission should establish guidelines for when reconciliations should be completed and update their policy manual to reflect best practices.
